archetypes.name: scope-control
archetypes.rationale: Checks that the plan stays within the three approved issue items and does not reintroduce excluded item-2 or broad help/ship-driver work.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the written plan matches the staged issue scope and approved direction, especially the explicit exclusion of item 2 and the non-goals around broad --help overhaul, python/ship.py contract pinning, and ship-path behavior changes. Look for planned files, tests, or documentation edits that exceed the approved three DX/doc-hardening fixes or add machinery not justified by the issue. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: Targets mismatches between planned shell contracts, docs, tests, Makefile wiring, and agent-lint exclusions across the touched scripts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare each planned script contract against its sibling documentation, existing harness expectations, Makefile targets, and lint configuration to find drift before implementation. Pay special attention to emitted key ordering, exit codes, source-vs-exec behavior, Bash 3.2 compatibility, and whether new sibling markdown files and Makefile-only exclusions are actually necessary and consistently named. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: orchestrator-dx
archetypes.rationale: Reviews whether the plan truly removes prompt-side orchestration friction without creating new fragile Step 0 or Step 5 invocation assumptions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan’s Step 0 and Step 5 changes as operator-experience contracts, not runtime feature work. Check whether self-deriving CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, exporting it, computing the Step 5 banner in one subprocess, and calling the new degraded-round CLI are aligned with existing skill text and avoid the exact prompt-side bash reimplementation failures described in the issue. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
